subject: sociology
title: Sociological Perspectives: Functionalism & Marxism
welcome_lead: Consensus vs conflict — the two big macro-frames.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology perspectives functionalism Durkheim Marxism Marx Althusser.
final_note: Same society, two very different stories.

concepts.def: Shared values bind society — functionalist view.
Society like a body — organs/institutions interdependent.
Society shaped by struggle between groups.
Althusser — schools, media, family — produce ideology.

walkthroughs.body_html: Durkheim (1893): society is held together by collective conscience. Parsons (1951): society like an organism with subsystems performing AGIL — Adaptation, Goal attainment, Integration, Latency. Merton (1949): distinguished manifest from latent functions and identified dysfunctions.

Marx (1867): history is class struggle. The base (economy) shapes the superstructure (politics, law, ideas). Capitalism extracts surplus value from workers. Lenin added imperialism analysis; Gramsci emphasised hegemony — rule through consent.

Althusser (1971): state controls via RSA (repressive — police, army) and ISA (ideological — schools, family, media, religion). Education is now the chief ISA. Ideology hides exploitation by making it seem natural and inevitable.

mcqs.q: Parsons's AGIL framework stands for what?
Althusser identified which two types of state apparatus?

numericals.q: In what year did Althusser publish his essay on ideological state apparatuses?

free_texts.q: Whose concept is 'hegemony' — ruling-class dominance through consent?
